summary: Verified WAFLOW login flow end-to-end on BOTH preview (https://new-app-builder-28.preview.emergentagent.com) and production (https://new-app-builder-28.emergent.host) URLs with credentials fascinadsagency@gmail.com / fascinads2026. Login succeeds cleanly on both environments. Backend /api/auth/login returns HTTP 200 with valid user object (curl + browser). Frontend correctly transitions from LoginWall to dashboard (login form disappears, project cards + flow editor visible). No 'body stream already read' TypeError. No console page-errors. No login-error data-testid element appears.
action_items: Login is fully functional from an automated browser perspective. The user's inability to log in is NOT a frontend/backend code bug.

Suggest to user: (1) Have them open DevTools > Application > Clear site data for BOTH domains and try again. (2) Disable browser password manager autofill and manually type 'fascinads2026' (their manager may have cached an older password). (3) Try Chrome Incognito with all extensions disabled — password managers, ad-blockers, and Grammarly can interfere with the /api/auth/login fetch. (4) Verify their browser is not blocking third-party cookies (needed for credentials: 'include' session cookie). (5) Ask them to share a screenshot of the exact 'login-error' text they see — the data-testid is 'login-error' inside a red box; if they never see that box, the request is not even being sent (extension/adblock blocking POST).

Consider adding a network-level catch in LoginWall that surfaces fetch TypeError (e.g. 'Failed to fetch', 'NetworkError') as a user-friendly Spanish message so the user can report WHICH class of failure they're hitting.
critical_code_review_comments: LoginWall.jsx submit() logic is robust: response.clone() before .text(), cache: no-store, submittingRef guard for StrictMode, credentials: include, no double-await. Implementation is correct.

One minor UX observation: when fetch itself throws (network offline, extension abort), the catch block sets err = e.message which for TypeError shows 'Failed to fetch' — English and unhelpful for a Spanish user. Consider mapping common network errors to Spanish.
test_credentials: fascinadsagency@gmail.com / fascinads2026 — verified working on both URLs
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login flow is verified working on preview + production. Backend responds HTTP 200, frontend transitions to dashboard successfully. If user still reports 'no puedo entrar', the root cause is client-side environmental (browser cache, autofilled wrong password, extension blocking POST, third-party cookies disabled). Not a code bug.
rca of the issue: No code-level bug reproducible. Backend /api/auth/login returns 200 with correct user payload for fascinadsagency@gmail.com/fascinads2026 in both preview and production. Frontend LoginWall.jsx correctly clones the response, parses JSON, calls setUser(data.user) and refresh(), which unmounts LoginWall and mounts the dashboard. Playwright reproduces the successful flow deterministically. Reproduction steps: (1) navigate to either URL, (2) fill login-email-input + login-password-input, (3) click login-submit-btn, (4) observe HTTP 200, form removed, dashboard rendered. Mitigation for the user: clear site data, disable password manager autofill (likely filling an old password), test in incognito with extensions off, verify third-party cookies not blocked.
